competences: The learner read and spell future-time vocabulary.
The learner use future-time words in meaningful sentences.
languageCompetence: Pronounces, reads, spells and uses correctly: tomorrow, next week, next month, next year, shan’t, won’t.
objectives: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to read and spell future-time vocabulary.
By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to use future-time words in meaningful sentences.
priorKnowledge: Learners know days of the week and can read familiar action words.
materials: Source sentence-builder table with will and shall
references: P 4 ENG & SST Lesson Notes Term III 2023
P 4 Composition AND Comprehension Scheme Term III

steps.content: Learners know days of the week and can read familiar action words. Key words: tomorrow, next week, next month, next year, shan’t, won’t
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher displays future-time vocabulary flashcards and links the chart to the prior knowledge: Learners know days of the week and can read familiar action words. The teacher pronounces the lesson vocabulary, checks learners’ reading, and introduces future-time vocabulary.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners recall familiar words, read the displayed key words aloud, and explain what they already know about the topic.

steps.content: Future-time words: tomorrow next week next month next year
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher models reading of this content: tomorrow next week next month next year The teacher checks pronunciation and meaning, draws attention to the target wording, and asks: "Construct a meaningful sentence using tomorrow." Learners’ responses are checked against the displayed text.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source sentences or entries aloud, identify the target words, answer the teacher’s question, and copy the stated content accurately.

steps.content: Negative forms: shall not will not shan’t won’t
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher models reading of this content: shall not will not shan’t won’t The teacher checks pronunciation and meaning, draws attention to the target wording, and asks: "Construct a meaningful sentence using next week." Learners’ responses are checked against the displayed text.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source sentences or entries aloud, identify the target words, answer the teacher’s question, and copy the stated content accurately.

steps.content: Example 1: Jane will go to school tomorrow. We shall not go to the market next week.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher models reading of this content: Jane will go to school tomorrow. We shall not go to the market next week. The teacher checks pronunciation and meaning, draws attention to the target wording, and asks: "Use the sentence table to write five sentences with shall, shall not, will or will not." Learners’ responses are checked against the displayed text.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source sentences or entries aloud, identify the target words, answer the teacher’s question, and copy the stated content accurately.

source.quote: Jane will go to school tomorrow

steps.content: Example 2: We shall not play with him. We shall go with him. We shall see lions, chimpanzees and monkeys. We shall come back home in the evening.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher models reading of this content: We shall not play with him. We shall go with him. We shall see lions, chimpanzees and monkeys. We shall come back home in the evening. The teacher checks pronunciation and meaning, draws attention to the target wording, and asks: "Use the sentence table to write five sentences with shall, shall not, will or will not." Learners’ responses are checked against the displayed text.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source sentences or entries aloud, identify the target words, answer the teacher’s question, and copy the stated content accurately.

source.quote: We shall not play with him

steps.content: Construct a meaningful sentence using tomorrow. Construct a meaningful sentence using next week. Use the sentence table to write five sentences with shall, shall not, will or will not.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher gives the following sourced text-based exercise: Construct a meaningful sentence using tomorrow. Construct a meaningful sentence using next week. Use the sentence table to write five sentences with shall, shall not, will or will not. The teacher checks learners’ written answers for meaning, spelling and punctuation, using this key: Source model: Jane will go to school tomorrow. Other meaningful sentences using tomorrow are acceptable. Source model: We shall not go to the market next week. Other meaningful sentences using next week are acceptable. Accept five grammatical combinations from the source table; for example, We shall go with him. We shall not play with him.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer individually in their books, use full sentences when required, read selected answers aloud, and correct spelling or punctuation after feedback.

source.quote: Use the vocabulary above to construct meaningful sentences

steps.content: Key answers: Source model: Jane will go to school tomorrow. Other meaningful sentences using tomorrow are acceptable. Source model: We shall not go to the market next week. Other meaningful sentences using next week are acceptable. Accept five grammatical combinations from the source table; for example, We shall go with him. We shall not play with him.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher revisits these questions: Construct a meaningful sentence using tomorrow. Construct a meaningful sentence using next week. Use the sentence table to write five sentences with shall, shall not, will or will not. The teacher checks whether learners have met the objectives, explains any remaining errors using the source text, and assigns the final exercise item for correction.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners explain their answers with evidence from the text, read corrected sentences aloud, and note the final item for homework.

source.quote: Look at the table below and write five sentences

assessment: Check oral reading and written responses to these questions: Construct a meaningful sentence using tomorrow. Construct a meaningful sentence using next week. Use the sentence table to write five sentences with shall, shall not, will or will not. Mark meaning, spelling, sentence structure and punctuation against the displayed source models.
homework: Complete or correct the following source exercise item, writing the answer neatly: Use the sentence table to write five sentences with shall, shall not, will or will not.
